table: Table 14 (Single-Equation Model Results, Staggered DiD columns, Study 3)
replication_status: exact (did::att_gt, not-yet-treated, universal base, no covariates, on the prepared panel with the last period t_idx = 170 dropped, aggte(type = 'calendar') = 0.08995803798, equal to the authors' staggered_cs calendar estimate to 2e-08 relative; aggte simple = 0.08986564649, equal to their simple estimate; scratchpad/meta4/v01572_did.R/.csv)
notes: Code/Staggered_code.R line 163: staggered_cs(i=seller_item, t=time_pre_post, g=happen_pre_post, y=valence, estimand='simple'). Outcome: product rating score (Study 3). P1 (days 1-85) vs P3 (original days 221-305 re-indexed to 86-170, post-enforcement); t = time_pre_post. The published estimate is the Callaway-Sant'Anna ATT from the Roth-Sant'Anna 'staggered' package (not-yet-treated controls; calendar aggregation: equal-weight average over calendar periods of the cohort-size-weighted ATT(g,t)), NOT a TWFE coefficient; the paper reports no TWFE for this design, so the TWFE here is the constructed counterpart y ~ D | seller_item + day, cluster seller_item, D = 1[t >= g]. staggered_cs plug-in SE printed as 0 in the authors' log; published_se is the Neyman SE. g_adopt = happen_* with the never-treated code (last period, 165 always-fast items) set to NA. Adoption = first day the item is a slow-delivery item (>3 days) in the post window, coded as absorbing by the authors although 4-5 percent of post-adoption item-days revert to fast delivery (not dropped, to match the reported spec). Balanced panel of 8,220 items. Cohort 86 (announcement day) holds >90 percent of treated items. 'preferred' follows the screening record (saleslog is the paper's focal outcome); within the paper the staggered DiD is a robustness variant of a two-group single-date DiD. AUTHORS' CSA SETTINGS (PROTOCOL 5b Hull alignment (c), Nov 2): the authors code never-treated items as cohort g = T (the last period, t_idx 170), so staggered_cs has no control at t = T and every cell at T drops out; this is implemented as sample_filter t_idx <= 169, applied to all three estimators (the 165 never-fast items are then never-treated, g_adopt = NA). The printed estimand is 'calendar', so csa_aggregation = 'calendar' (did aggte type 'calendar'). Superseded: published_coef/se previously held the simple estimand from the log (kept as authors_rerun_staggered_simple_*).
replication_note: Authors' staggered_cs re-run with R package staggered 1.2.2 on the shipped CSV reproduces the logged simple, cohort and calendar estimates to all printed digits (_work/authors_staggered_rerun.csv for simple).
published_source: Article (Management Science, Articles in Advance 2026) Table 14, Staggered DiD, P1 vs. P3, row Valence: 0.08996 (0.0278). The printed numbers are staggered_cs(estimand = 'calendar') with the Neyman SE, not estimand 'simple': the authors' Output/Staggered_results.log gives calendar 0.08995804 (se_neyman 0.02779935) vs simple 0.08986565; all 14 printed values match calendar, none match simple.
csa_weights_note: Nov 2: the published CSA comes from R did (or staggered, whose estimates did reproduces), which weights cells by fixed cohort shares; Hull's DiD-averaging weights cells by treated-observation counts. 'did' reproduces the published number (main analysis, option B); the strict-Hull run (CSA_STRICT_HULL=1, option A) ignores this field.
